model_completeness.definition: All eight contribution-account categories contain sourced or labeled modeled values, and GDP, employment, and wage county-comparison modules are populated. Comparison gaps are descriptive and do not establish causal facility effects.

research_value: Exact-address campus history; recurring operating activity and property-tax research.

history.date_note: This is a stored historical observation. Completion, grand opening, lease and operating-by dates are not automatically commissioning dates. Campus timing does not date every building.

research_updates.title: County accounts resolve the Houston I parcel and equipment history
research_updates.notes: Montgomery CAD identifies parcel 9714-07-00103 at 4001 Technology Forest Drive and reports IP Stream Houston LLC as owner through 2025; the 2026 row names Woodlands Industrial Development LLC. The Tax Office supplies verified parcel-account payments. A separate IP Stream Houston LLC account covers tanks, generators, machinery and equipment. Its older legal description names a 4001 Research Forest disaster recovery center but the account displays no situs, so its values and payments remain a separately labeled series. Appraised values are stocks, payments are account transactions, and neither establishes causal effects of the 2013 opening.

source.title: Montgomery Central Appraisal District property search — Stream Houston real and business-personal-property accounts
source.notes: The public appraisal search identifies real-property parcel 9714-07-00103 at 4001 Technology Forest Drive and reports annual land, improvement, market and appraised values. It separately identifies IP Stream Houston LLC business-personal-property account P454338 for tanks, generators, machinery and equipment. The personal-property account has no displayed situs; its 2015–2023 legal descriptions call it a disaster recovery center at 4001 Research Forest. Only value-ready 2014–2025 real-property rows and 2015–2025 personal-property rows are retained; the unfinished 2027 row is excluded.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Public-source review for the Microsoft facility at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. The exact-site ordinance and permit records are retained separately from later company/county and Greater San Antonio disclosures. Permit value is an administrative construction amount, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and water use is a source projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this building. Actual annual construction spending, worker residence, payroll, vendor payments, operating purchases, recipient-level tax receipts, same-scope public-service cost, electricity use, wastewater, emissions, and annual community transfers remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: DET01-specific direct-evidence follow-up. The operator data sheet supplies current facility-area and rated-power observations at 21005 Lahser Road. The 2014 operator release bounds the initial launch chronology but supplies no quantitative construction, supplier, payroll, community-funding, resource-use or public-cost observation. The values below are source-reported specifications, not audited utilization, expenditure or impact measures. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Public-source follow-up adds one facility-level 2024 electricity observation from Meta's environmental data index. The same source's rounded Forest City water-withdrawal and Scope 2 emissions values remain contextual until compatible canonical metric definitions exist. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Permit values are administrative amounts and are not summed because overlapping scopes cannot be ruled out. Assessment values are parcel stocks, not investment or tax receipts. The 125 acre-foot water right is regulatory capacity, not measured use. Food Bank gifts are company-region transfers, not campus-attributable annual spending. Vendor payments, worker residence, taxes received by jurisdiction, realized 2024 abatement, same-scope public-service cost, wastewater, and building-level electricity or water remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. The 2022 ownership transfer, assessments, estimated permit values, tax payments and hiring plan remain non-additive. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Low-confidence completion account for Microsoft San Antonio. Construction scenarios apply explicit 25%-75% construction-eligible shares to the reported greater-than-$840 million real-and-personal-property floor before using the Prince William County benchmark, so IT equipment is not silently treated as building construction. Operating scenarios combine the reported greater-than-75 employee floor with zero, half, or all of the separate 20-job expansion forecast; they are sensitivities, not fulfillment findings. County GDP, employment, and wage gaps are descriptive 2024 benchmark comparisons and are not facility effects. Existing source projections cover fiscal revenue, public support, and facility water demand. No annual net-fiscal estimate is made because verified same-scope recurring receipts and marginal public-service costs are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: DET01 completed contribution account. Source forecasts remain forecasts; modeled construction, supplier, household, resource and comparison values are visibly labeled sensitivity or benchmark scenarios. Personal-property equipment is excluded before construction multipliers. The 2025 tax-account aggregation is paired with an equal same-scope public-cost break-even threshold, not a net-fiscal result. County comparisons are descriptive and noncausal. Direct community funding, measured resource use, realized jobs, supplier payments and actual public costs remain gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Completed contribution-account syntheses for Meta Forest City / Rutherford County. Broad cumulative capital receives an explicit 25-75% construction-eligible allocation before transferred construction benchmarks; operating scenarios translate the 2015 reported-position snapshot with a visible FTE sensitivity; the same-county, same-fiscal-year tax and incentive claims are reconciled before the public-cost break-even threshold; facility water and electricity resource models retain source rounding and scope; supplier and household channels remain separate; and county comparisons are descriptive benchmark gaps rather than causal effects. No net fiscal, audited, or causal result is asserted. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution.
